findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the 'last-block-wins' claim with `_candidate_dicts` candidate ordering (fenced-group-then-object-group is not document order): either narrow to a SINGLE marker region (the last complete block only) before running the pipeline, or enforce true document-order last-wins over the marker regions, and add a test with a fence-wrapped LAST-block payload plus a bare EARLIER-block object.
evidence: _candidate_dicts (src/rebar/llm/structured.py:275-288): `for match in _FENCE_RE.finditer(text): candidates.append(...)` runs BEFORE `candidates.extend(_all_json_objects(text)[-32:])` before `candidates.append(whole)` — fenced candidates are grouped ahead of balanced-object candidates, not interleaved in document order
parse_structured last-valid-wins (:319-334) iterates that grouped `survivors` order, so 'last candidate' is last-in-group, not last-in-document
Plan quote: 'in document order, so the LAST block's object is naturally the last candidate and wins'
Plan AC/test explicitly includes the mixed case: 'marker block containing a fenced object -> payload still wins' and 'multiple blocks -> LAST wins'
findings.finding: The plan's 'last-block-wins' guarantee assumes document order is preserved when today's pipeline runs over the concatenated marker regions, but `_candidate_dicts` does not preserve document order: it emits ALL fenced-block candidates first, then all balanced-object candidates, then the whole-text candidate, and last-valid-wins iterates that grouped order. When the LAST marker block's payload is fence-wrapped and an EARLIER block's payload is a bare object (or vice-versa), the two blocks land in different candidate groups, document order is broken across groups, and an EARLIER block can win — contradicting the stated 'the LAST block's object is naturally the last candidate and wins.'
findings.location: Approach section ('run over the CONCATENATED marker-region text (in document order, so the LAST block's object is naturally the last candidate and wins)') and the fenced-object test in Testing
scenarios: A compliant reply emits two marker blocks where the model fence-wraps the payload in the LAST block (```json ...```) but rendered an earlier block's object bare — the earlier bare object wins instead of the intended last block
The E2 fenced-quote hazard combined with two marker blocks, where fence grouping reorders the intended last-block payload relative to an earlier candidate
findings.suggested_fix: State that front-narrowing scopes to the LAST complete marker block's region only (not the concatenation of all regions) — then 'last block wins' holds regardless of _candidate_dicts' fence/object grouping, because only one block's candidates are present. Add a pin: two marker blocks, LAST block fence-wrapped payload + EARLIER block bare object -> the last block's payload wins.
